buyer_groups.group_title: 1. 外資大戶：AI概念股與航空雙主流，ETF避險兼布局

stocks.description: 肖年仔，你看外資狂掃 55.3萬張 0050，這不是在跟你開玩笑，這是標準的避險兼布局！大盤震盪，先買ETF穩住陣腳，等風頭過了再說，這就是大戶的智慧，不是你那種黑白買的韭菜思維。
記憶體族群最近有點動靜，外資買超 2.5萬張 華邦電，這擺明是看好後市，或是跟著AI題材在卡位，肖年仔，這不是讓你去接刀的，是看主力怎麼玩。
AI概念股的指標，外資再買 1.3萬張 緯創，這檔老牌電子股被AI點火後，籌碼還在持續鎖碼中，但漲多就是風險，別傻傻追高被倒貨。
航空雙雄之一，外資買超 1.3萬張 長榮航，解封題材還在燒，但投信卻在賣，這就是外資跟內資的看法分歧，肖年仔，別被兩邊的動作搞糊塗了。
跟長榮航一樣，外資也買超 1.0萬張 華航，這波航空股的熱度，外資顯然還想再炒一波，但投信也在出貨，小心隔日沖的賣壓。

buyer_groups.group_title: 2. 投信大戶（本土國家隊）：金融股作帳行情，AI概念股持續加碼

stocks.description: 外資狂倒 8.9萬張 聯電，結果投信卻逆勢買超 1.4萬張，這擺明是投信在撿便宜，或是看好成熟製程的低基期，肖年仔，這就是籌碼換手，看誰笑到最後。
外資大賣 4.9萬張 南亞，投信卻買超 1.3萬張，這跟聯電一樣，都是內外資對傳產股的看法不同調，投信可能在作帳，也可能看好塑化股的谷底翻身。
投信買超 1.0萬張 凱基金，金融股在月底作帳行情中，投信常常會拉抬自家或關係企業的股票，肖年仔，這就是國家隊的玩法。
AI概念股緯創，投信也買超 0.9萬張，跟外資同步加碼，這表示AI題材還是主流，但漲多風險高，別當最後一隻老鼠。
投信買超 0.8萬張 華南金，金融股的作帳行情持續，這也是避險資金的去處，但別期待會有什麼噴出行情。

buyer_groups.group_title: 3. 內資主力與實戶：鎖定金融、營建與中小型科技股

stocks.description: 自營商買超 0.13萬張 第一金，外資卻大賣，這就是內資主力在玩短線，金融股波動小，適合隔日沖或短線進出，肖年仔，別以為有什麼大利多。
營建股愛山林，自營商買超 0.09萬張，這波營建股有特定題材在炒作，內資主力喜歡這種股性活潑的標的，但風險也高，小心被套牢。
自營商也買超 0.05萬張 華邦電，跟外資同步，顯示記憶體族群的確有資金在關注，但自營商的動作常常是避險盤，別太認真。
封測股南茂，自營商買超 0.04萬張，這就是內資主力在找低基期或有轉機的中小型科技股，但這種股票籌碼輕，容易被拉高出貨。
AI概念股緯創，自營商也買超 0.03萬張，三大法人都同步買進，但自營商的量不大，可能只是跟單或避險操作。

strategies.strategy_title: 策略一：高檔避險與資金避風港（ETF、金融）
strategies.strategy_content: 肖年仔，你看外資狂掃 0050 這麼多，這不是沒有道理的。大盤在高檔震盪，美股那邊巴菲特都說要買S&P 500 ETF了，外資買 0050 就是標準的避險操作，把資金停泊在指數型基金，避免個股波動風險。同時，投信和自營商也同步加碼金融股，這除了有作帳的考量，也是在尋找相對穩定的避風港，畢竟金融股的股性相對溫和，適合在市場不確定時作為防禦性配置。

strategies.strategy_title: 策略二：AI概念股持續點火，但籌碼開始換手
strategies.strategy_content: AI題材還是市場主流，緯創、英業達、華邦電這些AI概念股，外資和投信都還在買超，顯示資金對這個板塊的熱情還沒退燒。但肖年仔，你要注意，像聯電這種，外資大賣，投信卻大買，這就是籌碼在換手。外資可能覺得漲夠了要獲利了結，投信則可能是看好低基期或有轉機的半導體股。這時候就考驗你的眼光了，別傻傻地去接外資倒出來的貨。

strategies.strategy_title: 策略三：內外資對傳產與部分金融看法分歧，小心隔日沖
strategies.strategy_content: 航空雙雄長榮航、華航，外資大買，但投信卻在賣，這就是內外資對解封題材的看法不同調。外資可能想再炒一波，但投信可能覺得漲幅已高，開始獲利了結。另外，像南亞、臺企銀這些傳產和金融股，外資大賣，投信卻有買進，這也顯示了市場資金的拉扯。肖年仔，這種內外資對作的股票，常常是隔日沖的最愛，今天買明天倒，你一不小心就會被割韭菜。

stock_uncle_insight.summary: 肖年仔，今天市場就是一個字：亂！外資避險兼布局AI和航空，投信作帳兼撿低基期，內資主力則在金融營建裡玩短線。籌碼換手頻繁，別傻傻追高，小心被主力拉高出貨！

top_brokerages_analysis.uncle_logic: 高盛狂買 0050，這就是外資大戶的標準避險動作，看好台股長期趨勢，但短期震盪先用ETF穩住，肖年仔，這不是讓你去追個股的訊號。
凱基台北買第一金，這分點是出了名的隔日沖大戶，買金融股這種波動小的標的，擺明就是想賺個價差就跑，肖年仔，別傻傻地跟著進去當接刀俠。
元大投信買聯電，這就是本土國家隊在作帳，同時也可能是看好半導體成熟製程的低基期，跟外資對作，看誰的眼光比較準。
摩根大通大賣聯電，這跟高盛買 0050 形成對比，外資大戶對聯電的看法分歧，可能是獲利了結，也可能是轉往其他AI概念股，肖年仔，這就是大戶的資金挪移，你得看清楚。

english_professor_news.title: Warren Buffett keeps pointing at the same ETF for a reason

level1_blind.text:
Most people assume that the world's most successful investors have some edge that regular people can't access. Better information. Smarter models. A network of insiders who call before the news breaks. Warren Buffett spent 60 years proving that assumption wrong, building one of the greatest fortunes in history through patience and simplicity rather than complexity.

And yet when people ask him what they should do with their money, his answer has been the same for decades. It's not a stock tip. It's not a sector call. It's an ETF that anyone can buy for three cents on every hundred dollars invested.

Buffett has made his position clear in shareholder letters, interviews, and annual meetings going back years. In his 2016 shareholder letter, he wrote: "My regular recommendation has been a low-cost S&P 500index fund." At Berkshire's 2021 annual meeting, he said: "In my view, for most people, I think that the best thing to do is buy an S&P 500 index fund."

The most direct version of the advice came in his 2013 letter to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders, where he described the instructions he had written into his will for the money he would leave to his wife: "My advice to the trustee could not be more simple: Put 10% of the cash in short-term government bonds and 90% in a very low-cost S&P 500 index fund. (I suggest Vanguard's.) I believe the trust's long-term results from this policy will be superior to those attained by most investors, whether pension funds, institutions or individuals, who employ high-fee managers," according to The Motley Fool.

He wasn't being modest. He was being precise. This is the same man who beat the market by an enormous margin over six decades, and he was saying that for his own wife's trust, a simple index fund would beat most professional managers.

Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) tracks the S¼P 500, charges 0.03% a year, and has grown to more than $950 billion in assets. Three cents on every hundred dollars. On a $10,000 investment that's $3 annually in fees. That's it. That's what Buffett means when he says low cost, and that's why he keeps naming Vanguard specifically when people ask which fund.

VOO gives investors exposure to 500 of America's largest companies across all 11 sectors of the economy, from technology and healthcare to energy and consumer staples. The top holdings include Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple, Amazon, and Alphabet. Any component that deteriorates over time gets removed and replaced. The index self-corrects without the investor having to do anything.

VOO has averaged about 15% annual growth over the past decade. Nobody enjoyed the 2020 crash while it was happening. Or any of the other rough patches in between. But the return is what you get if you didn't sell, and most of the people who did sell locked in losses they never recovered.

english_professor_news.title: Cathie Wood sells $5.5 million of surging tech stock
english_professor_news.level1_blind:
Cathie Wood, head of Ark Investment Management, likes to lock in gains when her tech darlings rally.

That's exactly what she's doing with Snowflake, trimming her position after the cloud software stock surged nearly 10% over the past five trading days ahead of earnings.

In 2025, the flagship Ark Innovation ETF gained 35.49%, far outpacing the S&P 500's return of 17.88% in the same period. But so far this year, Wood's flagship Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK) is down 8.51% as of July 31, while the S&P 500 surged 9.41%, Yahoo Finance data shows.

Wood gained a reputation after the Ark Innovation ETF delivered a 153% return in 2020. But her style also brings painful losses in bearish markets, as seen in 2022, when the Ark Innovation ETF tumbled more than 60%.

Those swings have weighed on Wood's long-term gains. As of July 31, her Ark Innovation ETF has delivered a five-year annualized return of -9.75%, while the S&P 500 has an annualized return of 11.25% over the same period, according to data from Morningstar.

Wood usually focuses on high-tech companies across artificial intelligence, blockchain, biomedical technology, and robotics. She believes these businesses have strong growth potential, though their volatility often causes fluctuations in the Ark's funds.

Over the decade ended 2025, the Ark Innovation ETF wiped out nearly $5 billion in investor wealth, according to an analysis by Morningstar's analyst Amy Arnott. That made it the fourth-biggest wealth destroyer among mutual funds and ETFs in the ranking.

Wood believes investors have been focusing on the wrong signals as they assess the outlook for inflation, interest rates, and stocks.

english_professor_news.title: CoreWeave Just Scored a Leidos Partnership. What That Means for CRWV Stock Here.

level1_blind.text:
Neocloud provider CoreWeave (CRWV) saw its stock rise by 21.5% intraday on July 30 as the company announced a partnership with Leidos Holdings (LDOS) to provide artificial intelligence (AI) cloud services to United Stated federal agencies, so that they can deploy and operate AI at mission scale. This extends CoreWeave's reach into addressing U.S. Intelligence Community (IC) and Department of Defense's (DoD) unique requirements.

This also diversifies CoreWeave's customer base, as government contracts bring stability and are spread across a broad number of agencies, which is important for a company that relies on its top customers for a major portion of its revenue.

Moreover, there's a threat looming of a customer turning into a potential rival. Meta Platforms (META) is reportedly entering the neocloud business, with its massive cash hoard and industry-wide reach. In Q1, CoreWeave executed multiple new agreements with Meta, including a new $21 billion commitment signed in March.

On the other hand, the neocloud business is thriving, with providers expected to capture 20% of the $267 billion AI cloud market by 2030, as per Gartner. Therefore, established neocloud providers like CoreWeave have significant prospects in the market, and the Leidos partnership is a possible testament to that.

CoreWeave is a cloud infrastructure company focused on providing GPU-powered computing for AI developers and enterprises. It operates data centers across the U.S. and Europe, with a platform designed to support large-scale training and deployment of generative AI workloads.
